relationships.title: Re: Sub-IPC on Tech Atrocity Prevention Key Events
relationships.evidence:
[opaque block] [opaque block]
Hi everyone,
I had a talk with Garth who works with Vera, the Agency MDM lead and is coordinating
the response to this NSC request.
1. We both think it is a good opportunity to engage tech companies in addressing
MDM ahead of elections/critical events.
1. The term 'atrocity prevention' can sound shocking but the framework is similar to
other conflict/violence prevention frameworks including USAID's election security
and election assessment frameworks. Similar to the term anti-corruption, care has
to be used when discussing the issue and using the term with local partners.
1. Garth and his State department counterpart will put forward five countries including
Bangladesh and Burma for consideration to NSC with the caveat that additional
consultation/approval is needed with missions/embassies and regional bureaus.
Theywill also recommend that NSC chooses one country to focus on as a test
case/proof of concept while watching the other four for possible engangement.
Other countries are Zimbabwe, El Salvador, and the Democratic Republic of
Congo.
1.If missions agree, I think we should advocate for an Asia country to get selected,
perhaps Burma given the recent request from AA Schiffer regarding Burma
elections.

DDI/DRG Center and CPS (I think) are leading out on USAID's contribution to a Sub-IPC on Engagement of
Tech Companies and Atrocity Prevention. They have identified 8 countries (Burma, Bangladesh, Pakistan,
Zimbabwe, Democratic Republic of Congo, Ethiopia, Mali and El Salvador) that will be narrowed down to
